geometry_edits.rationale: Retarget the dominant mass from a generic field to a split-wing cultural figure that can generate a court and public sequence.
Use a split layout to create a clearer open middle condition instead of a sealed block.
Align the split/opening logic to the verified access side in the program frame.
Open a civic gap large enough to read as a public void rather than a mere crack.
Keep the connector thin so the two wings remain legible and the void retains public character.
Introduce a ground spine to strengthen entry sequence and public threshold at the base.
Preserve the access-aligned lift logic on the program-frame west side.
Increase the lift so the access edge becomes a clearer undercut/entry seam.

graph_edits.rationale: The current dominant mass reads as a generic compact block; split-wing is a better cultural massing move to create a readable public sequence and separate civic/support bodies.
Increase offset to break the blocky repetition and produce a clearer stepped/open rhythm.
Loosen the massing field to allow a more legible carved court or public seam.
Keep the threshold aligned to the verified access relation; the public response should open on the access-facing side.
Strengthen the lifted public threshold so the access edge becomes a readable undercut or lifted seam.
Slightly increase support presence to make the lifted civic edge clearer without collapsing the ground response.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent compact bar in all four views, so it is not rejected for inconsistency, but it is still underdeveloped for the cultural brief. The mass is heavily blocky with repetitive vertical articulations and only shallow internal voiding visible in plan; there is no strong public court, carved sequence, or daylight-oriented section. The verified access edge is acknowledged only weakly: the blue frontage line sits beside the parcel, but the building does not clearly open toward it with a legible ground threshold, entry seam, or undercut. Compared with the references, it has some resonance with compact cultural pavilions and terraced masses, but it lacks the public sequence, roof/section logic, and carved civic void that the brief requires. So it fails program_fit_hard_pass even though the geometry is stable and repairable.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced cultural landscape with carved public bowls, ramps, and layered open-to-solid hierarchy.
A dominant cantilevered civic mass can be paired with a clear public ground condition and a lighter support/core.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is office-like in its visible massing; use only the threshold logic, not the typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple monolithic massing can work if the access edge is expressed through a threshold, void, or bridge-like articulation.
Long horizontal cultural volumes with setbacks, bridge links, and courtyard-like voids support exhibition/public sequence.
Ring/terrace integration suggests landscape-responsive cultural massing and a readable carved-open center.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied in the visible views, but the access response is semantically weak.
The form is coherent across views, but the open-space figure is too shallow to carry the cultural/public-sequence brief.
Stepped/terraced appearance is present, yet it reads more as repetitive code-minimum massing than as an inhabited cultural section.
